h: Shoes, Saints and Mackintosh in Northampton
p: Northampton's shoemaking story runs deep, and the best place to see it is Northampton Museum and Art Gallery on Guildhall Road, home to a huge collection of footwear spanning centuries. It's free to visit and surprisingly fascinating, even for people who wouldn't call themselves shoe fans. Who knew trainers had such a history?

Design lovers shouldn't miss 78 Derngate, a terraced house remodelled by the famous Scottish designer Charles Rennie Mackintosh. It's his only major work in England, and the bold interiors are a real eye-opener. Next door, the Royal and Derngate theatre puts on drama, comedy and big touring shows.

Sports fans will know Northampton Saints, the town's top-flight rugby union side, and the atmosphere around their Franklin's Gardens ground is something to see on match days. For a family afternoon outdoors, Abington Park has lakes, play areas and an old manor house museum, while Delapré Abbey, on the south side of town, has gardens, woodland walks and centuries of history to dig into.

If you're travelling in, look out for the tall Northampton Lift Tower on the skyline. Locals call it the Northampton Lighthouse, despite the town being about as far from the sea as you can get in England.
